clue.text: Dirigible count?

definitions.meaning: a dirigible is a rigid airship of the kind built in Germany before the wars
Count Ferdinand von ..., the German nobleman who designed those airships

explanation.definitionFit: The airship took its name from the German count who invented it, so one word covers both the craft and the nobleman.

clue.text: He works with a will

parts.note: reads as an energetic worker, but the will is a legal testament and he carries out its terms

explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a testament to carry out its instructions after a death holds this legal title.

clue.text: Dispensed with formula

parts.note: reads as doing without a set method, but it is a chemist's written order that is dispensed by a pharmacist

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's written medical order is a formula that a pharmacist makes up and hands over, i.e. dispenses.

clue.text: Artist, about six, getting up full of energy

indicators.note: the painter's name goes round, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born portrait painter at the English court

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A painter of about six years old rises from bed bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns VI into IV, and 'about' puts the painter LELY around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lively is vigorous and animated, brimming with vitality.

clue.text: Celebrity in Latin America

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words Latin America, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A famous person living somewhere in Latin America.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a big name, someone well known.

clue.text: Tried the depth and got to the bottom of it

definitions.meaning: measured how deep water is, in units of six feet

definitions.text: got to the bottom of it

explanation.definitionFit: A nautical unit for sounding water gives a verb for measuring depth, and figuratively for understanding something deep.

clue.text: In Brittany, first person on the highway has something ludicrous

parts.note: JE is French for I, the first person pronoun, as spoken in Brittany in France
ST is the abbreviation for street, a public road

explanation.surface: A traveller in Brittany finds something absurd on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Brittany is a region of France, which is the cue to use the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or a jape is something laughable, said for fun rather than seriously.

clue.text: Station troops in a fortified town

definitions.meaning: a verb: to post soldiers somewhere to defend it
a defended stronghold manned by soldiers

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the act of posting soldiers in a place and the stronghold or force so posted.

clue.text: Name a hat possibly as an object of abhorrence

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise, signalling a reshuffle

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone names a particular hat as the thing they hate most.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema is intensely loathed, a thing cursed or detested.

clue.text: Apportion the main course, so to speak

indicators.note: signals the word is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: meat is the main dish at dinner

explanation.surface: Serving out the main dish of a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute shares of something.

clue.text: One who works at intervals on the stage

definitions.text: One who works at intervals on the stage

parts.words: One who works at intervals on the stage
parts.note: a stagehand who changes the sets between scenes and during the intervals of a play

explanation.definitionFit: A theatre stagehand moves the scenery between acts, which is when the curtain is down.

clue.text: Part of a horse sounds like all of it

indicators.note: signals that a phrase spoken aloud gives the answer

parts.note: four quarters together make up the whole of anything

explanation.surface: A riddle that one part of a horse sounds like the entire animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The front legs and shoulders of a horse are known collectively by this anatomical term.

clue.text: Floored, having noticed rot's developing first

indicators.note: the anagram comes first, ahead of the other piece
the letters of rot's are developing into a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here: rot is
eyed means looked at or noticed

explanation.surface: A floor was found to have rot spreading through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges ROTS into STOR, which 'first' places before EYED.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with floors at different levels is described by the number of its levels, so floored means having storeys.

clue.text: Doctor behind with payment

parts.note: aft means at the rear, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A doctor is late with his fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft is an order for payment of money, a form of cheque.

clue.text: Large quantity of gold in the swampy ground

indicators.note: the gold goes inside the large quantity

parts.note: a mass is a large amount
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A hoard of gold lies buried in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog or marsh, wet ground hard to cross.

clue.text: Envelop in snow rapidly

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the phrase snow rapidly

explanation.surface: Something quickly covered by falling snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to enfold or cover completely.

clue.text: Game-bird would sound like a rooster

indicators.note: signals that the first piece is heard rather than seen

parts.note: the word would is spoken aloud
a cock is a male chicken

explanation.surface: Pondering whether a game-bird might crow like a farmyard cockerel.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a wading bird shot for sport, hence game.

clue.text: Mark, British money!

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: An exclamation celebrating sterling cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a mark burned onto livestock, or a trademark.

clue.text: Note Edward had conferred a military rank on another

definitions.text: had conferred a military rank on another

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A man named Edward receives a note promoting another soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: A brevet is an army commission giving an officer a higher rank without the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To brevet is to promote an officer to a higher honorary rank, so this past tense means granted such a rank.

clue.text: A child of five

parts.note: reads as a five-year-old, but means one of five babies born at a single birth

explanation.definitionFit: A quintuplet, one of five siblings born together, is called by this short form.

clue.text: Having arrived to make an attack whilst taking control

parts.note: a person who is in has arrived home or at a place
to charge is to rush at an enemy

explanation.surface: Troops arrive and launch an assault to seize power.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in charge means being in command, holding authority over others.

clue.text: Work here no longer on the rocks

parts.note: something switched off is no longer on
a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: Someone whose job collapsed, like a marriage on the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place where people work, so 'work here' points to it.

clue.text: Ruler had the Yorkshire charter amended

parts.note: in Yorkshire dialect 'the' is shortened to t'

indicators.note: the letters are amended into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler had a county's founding charter rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire speech famously clips 'the' to t', so 'the Yorkshire' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrarch was a governor of a quarter of a Roman province, a minor ruler.

clue.text: I want a new name for the island

indicators.note: a new version of the letters, meaning they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the island to be renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwan is a large island off the coast of China.

clue.text: It's scored-by the opposition?

parts.note: musical lines set against each other are written out in a score

explanation.definitionFit: In music, independent melodies played against one another are written in a score, hence scored.

clue.text: As far as being aware of the latest developments

definitions.meaning: reaching a limit, as in counting to ten

definitions.text: being aware of the latest developments
definitions.meaning: well informed, as in being current with the news

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase marks a limit of extent, and also, as in up-to-date, means informed of current news.

clue.text: Healthy colour

explanation.definitionFit: The pale red shade gives the idiom in the pink, meaning in fine health.

clue.text: Swirling bore of European waterway

indicators.note: swirling letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A tidal surge sweeping along a river in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a major river in northern Spain.

clue.text: Whale can act strangely with ease, say

indicators.note: the letters are put together strangely, in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: signals the word is heard: spoken, ease sounds like E's, two letter E

parts.note: the word ease said aloud

explanation.surface: A whale is able to perform easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns 'ease' into its sound, two Es, which join CANACT for 'strangely' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cetacean is any member of the order of marine mammals that includes whales and dolphins.

clue.text: Actor found two books left you formerly returned

parts.note: First and Second Kings are two books of the Old Testament

indicators.note: the old word for you is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: An actor discovers two volumes left behind by someone long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Ben Kingsley is the actor; 'returned' turns YE into EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Kingsley is an Oscar-winning British actor, an example of the class.
